request:
Feature request: visits can currently only be created, never corrected. Two
product decisions come with it, made here as the product owner:

- Non-goal NG-5 is narrowed: cancelling a booked visit stays out of scope,
  but correcting its date and description is now in. Record the narrowing
  the way the project records non-goal changes.
- The edit form is reachable by its URL alone: the owner detail page gains
  no edit link in this request. A visible entry point may come as a
  follow-up request.

Add editing for a booked visit:

- GET /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit shows the visit
  form prefilled with that visit's current date and description. Reuse the
  existing visit form template (pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm) and its `visit`
  model attribute.
- POST to the same URL validates like visit creation (description required,
  date in the future). On success it updates that visit in place — the pet
  must not gain an additional visit record — and redirects to the owner
  detail page. On validation failure it redisplays the form.

Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Staff can correct a booked visit's date and description
summary: A booked visit can be corrected afterwards: its date and description change in place, held to the same bar as booking, without leaving the pet with a second visit.
acceptance_criteria: given a booked visit, when it is opened for correction, then the same form used for booking is shown carrying that visit's current date and description
given a booked visit, when a description and a date later than today are submitted, then that visit holds the submitted date and description and the owner's record is shown
given a booked visit, when a correction succeeds, then the number of visits recorded against the pet is unchanged
given a blank description, when the correction is submitted, then it is refused, the description is named, and the form is shown again
given a date of today or earlier, when the correction is submitted, then it is refused, the date is named, and the form is shown again
given a visit that does not belong to the named pet, or whose pet does not belong to the named owner, when correction is attempted, then it is refused
non_goals: cancelling or deleting a booked visit (NG-5, NG-4)
a visible route to the correction from the owner's record — the owner deferred the entry point to a possible follow-up request
changing which pet a visit belongs to
notes: Narrowing recorded in docs/adr/2026-09-06-non-goal-visit-correction-narrowing.md; the 2026-08-08 non-goal ADR's status line now points to it. The owner fixed the request address, the form template and its model attribute — quoted verbatim in the intake-decision at .scratch/handoff.jsonl line 2; design must honor them. Two open questions recorded in the PRD rather than escalated, per the owner's no-reply instruction: whether a visible entry point follows, and whether a past-dated visit should be correctable at all (REQ-VIS-003 applies the booking date bar unchanged, so it cannot keep its original date). docs/adr/README.md needs an index row for the new ADR; that file is outside the product expert's write scope.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Visit correction is the create-and-edit route pair PetController already demonstrates in the same package, applied to VisitController. No new module, pattern, dependency, or bounded context. One existing seam needs adjusting: the @ModelAttribute("visit") factory (VisitController.java:63) unconditionally constructs a Visit and attaches it to the pet, so it cannot serve the correction route unchanged. It becomes load-or-create keyed on an optional visitId path variable, exactly mirroring PetController.findPet (PetController.java:75). Basis for the covering claim is grep plus direct reads of VisitController, PetController, Owner, Pet, Visit and the form template — the IDE oracle is not connected in this run, which is the weaker basis. Durable memory covering the slice: system-design.md Overview (owner is the aggregate entry point; no VisitRepository; visits written through OwnerRepository cascade), Contracts (Invariants the rows cannot carry), and Package Structure. Design writes this dispatch: REQ-VIS-003 joins the Owner, Visit, OwnerRepository and VisitController Contracts rows; the Owner, Visit and VisitController purposes now name correction; the Invariants paragraph records that a visit is reached for correction through the root; docs/adr/README.md gains the index row for the 2026-09-06 non-goal ADR and marks the 2026-08-08 row narrowed.
integration_points: The @ModelAttribute("visit") factory serves both routes: it takes @PathVariable(name = "visitId", required = false) Integer visitId, returns the pet's existing visit when present, and keeps today's new-and-attach behavior when absent.

Binding lands on the persisted Visit instance held in pet.getVisits(), so the correction updates in place and the pet's visit count is unchanged; adding that same instance back to the LinkedHashSet is what must not happen on the correction path.
Write path is unchanged: owners.save(owner) cascades from the aggregate root. No VisitRepository is introduced.
The form template posts to the current URL (no th:action) and reads only visit, pet and owner from the model, all of which the factory already supplies. Expect no template change.
Both routes render the same view name, pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm, and redirect to redirect:/owners/{ownerId}.

patterns.description: findPet — load-or-create model attribute keyed on an optional path variable; the shape the visit factory adopts
initUpdateForm and processUpdateForm — the create-and-edit route pair on one controller, with the same view and redirect
the non-future-visit-date check the correction route shares rather than copies

risks.risk: Copying the non-future-date check into the correction handler writes a second business rule into a controller.
risks.mitigation: Extract the existing check into one private method called by both handlers. architecture-principles.md pattern catalog, Web controller row: 'A new rule added to a controller is a fresh violation, not covered by the existing one.' Do not relocate the rule to a Validator or a service — system-design.md Open Questions from the Survey item 2 leaves that placement undecided, and a feature slice does not settle it.

risks.risk: Rejecting the date with a fresh error code breaks the message bundles and the existing REQ-VIS-001 test, which asserts the code.
risks.mitigation: Keep result.rejectValue("date", "typeMismatch.visitDate") on both routes. REQ-LANG-002; VisitControllerTests.processNewVisitFormHasErrorsWhenVisitDateIsNotInFuture asserts that exact code.

risks.risk: A visitId not belonging to the named pet, or a pet not belonging to the named owner, is accepted and a foreign visit is rewritten.
risks.mitigation: Resolve the visit by scanning pet.getVisits() for the id inside the model-attribute factory, and throw IllegalArgumentException when it is absent — the same shape the factory already uses for a missing owner or pet. security-principles.md Realization, 'Trusting cross-request state': each request re-resolves and re-validates the entities it acts on. Resolution through the aggregate root makes containment structural rather than a check that can be forgotten.

risks.risk: Identifier binding on an edit route lets a submitted id repoint the persisted visit.
risks.mitigation: Keep the existing unnamed @InitBinder disallowing id and *.id; it applies to the correction route too. security-principles.md Realization, Mass assignment row.

risks.risk: A new exception message carries more than identifiers into the error page.
risks.mitigation: Put only the owner, pet and visit identifiers in the message. security-principles.md Realization, 'Secret disclosure through logs and errors' — the error page renders the exception message (system-design.md Known Defects).

risks.risk: The correction path constructs a detached Visit and saves it, leaving the pet with two visit rows.
risks.mitigation: Bind onto the instance the factory returned from pet.getVisits(); assert the pet's visit count in the test (PRD acceptance criterion 3). The test fixture holds real Owner and Pet objects, so the assertion reads the mutated instance directly — no argument captor needed.

notes:
Autofix audit: no design-doc-autofix records in the log; nothing to judge.

Open questions recorded, not decided — the owner stated no further product answer arrives this slice, so each takes the narrowest reading consistent with the request.
(1) No confirmation message. Booking adds a hard-coded flash string; the request asks only for the redirect, and new user-facing text would need a key in all eleven bundles (REQ-LANG-002). The correction adds none.
(2) The template keeps its booking wording. The submit label reads from the addVisit key and the heading drops 'New' when the visit is persisted; changing either needs the same eleven-bundle work and is outside this request.
(3) Past-dated visits. The booking date bar applies unchanged, so a visit whose date has passed cannot be corrected while keeping its date. The PRD records this; the design does not resolve it.
(4) No entry point. The owner detail template is untouched, per the recorded non-goal.

Brief follow-up for doc-sync, outside my write scope: architecture-principles.md line 91 lists the non-future-visit-date check among rules living in controller methods. That stays true under this design — the check is shared, not moved — so no edit is needed now. It would go stale the moment the placement open question is settled.

author: security-reviewer
recommendations: Mass-assignment surface carried over, not introduced: processUpdateVisitForm binds @ModelAttribute Owner owner from request parameters and then calls owners.save(owner), so a POST to /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit can also rewrite owner fields (firstName, lastName, address, city, telephone) and nested pet/visit fields that the correction form never posts. This mirrors processNewVisitForm exactly, and the application ships no authentication or authorization layer, so the endpoint grants an attacker nothing they cannot already obtain through /owners/{ownerId}/edit - reachability yields no privilege gain and the pattern is consistent with its neighbour, hence no fix demanded here. If a future slice adds an entry point, an auth layer, or narrows binding on one visit route, narrow both together (e.g. @InitBinder("owner") restricted to no bindable fields on the visit routes) so the two routes cannot drift apart.

Supply chain not verified against the NVD in this review: build.gradle configures no OWASP dependency-check plugin, and this reviewer has no network access, so no CVE matching ran. This is 'not run', not 'clean'. The change set alters no dependency declaration, so the slice adds no new artifact to check; a human or CI should close the standing check against the declared Spring Boot 4.1.0 stack.

No CSRF protection exists anywhere in the application (Spring Security is not on the classpath), so the new state-changing POST route inherits that gap along with every existing POST. Not a regression and not fixable inside this slice; worth naming if an authentication layer is ever added, at which point the visit-correction route needs the token like every other write.

The description column is VARCHAR(255) on H2 and MySQL while Visit.description carries only @NotBlank, so an over-long correction fails as a database integrity violation rather than a named field error. Pre-existing for booking and identical for correction; a @Size bound on the field would make both routes fail gracefully.
approved_aspects: Insecure direct object reference closed at the aggregate: findVisit(Pet, Integer, int) resolves the visit by streaming pet.getVisits(), so a visitId belonging to another pet or another owner is unreachable through the path; VisitControllerTests.theVisitCorrectionShouldBeRefusedWhenTheVisitBelongsToAnotherPet pins it, and the pet/owner mismatch still throws in loadPetWithVisit before any binding runs

Identifier tampering blocked: the pre-existing @InitBinder setDisallowedFields("id", "*.id") covers the new route because it is class-scoped and un-narrowed, so a submitted id parameter cannot repoint the bound Visit; theVisitCorrectionShouldIgnoreASubmittedIdentifier asserts it

Validation is not weakened on the write path: @Valid plus the shared rejectDateNotInFuture(Visit, BindingResult) applies the same @NotBlank description and future-date bar to correction as to booking, and both refusal paths return the form without reaching owners.save

No new injection surface: the change adds no shell execution, no string-built query, no file or path handling, no XML/JSON/YAML deserialization, no logging of request values, and no template change; visit.description continues to render through Thymeleaf th:text (escaped) in ownerDetails.html and createOrUpdateVisitForm.html

Persistence stays on the sanctioned single write path (OwnerRepository.save through the owner aggregate), matching the invariant recorded in docs/system-design.md; no direct visit lookup or repository was introduced
No credentials, tokens, or secrets in the diff; no hardcoded URLs; error text in the new IllegalArgumentException carries only entity ids, matching the existing loadPetWithVisit messages
No dependency, build, or configuration change in the change set, so the resolved artifact set is unchanged by this slice

The new createABookedVisit(LocalDate, String) factory method in VisitControllerTests replaces the direct new Visit() construction in @BeforeEach, following the Three-Tier/factory convention testing-principles.md requires; the method is small, single-purpose and named by role.

The new theVisitCorrectionShouldBeRefusedWhenThePetBelongsToAnotherOwner test follows the existing BDD naming and four-phase structure of its neighbours (theVisitCorrectionShouldBeRefusedWhenTheVisitBelongsToAnotherPet), reuses CORRECTED_DATE/CORRECTED_DESCRIPTION rather than new magic literals, and introduces no production code change.
No new business-rule placement, naming, or error-handling issues introduced by the fix delta; format check (./gradlew checkFormat) passes with no output.

author: change-grader
summary: add in-place correction of a booked visit

blast_radius.note: One module and one class: VisitController gains two routes and a private aggregate-walking lookup, with the docs half of the diff recording the NG-5 narrowing. No template, schema, dependency, or config change, no sensitive path, and the booking route is preserved because visitId is null there.

semantic_surprise.note: Reading the hunks, both refactors are faithful (the extracted rejectDateNotInFuture body is identical to the deleted inline check, and the view constant equals the literal it replaces), and findVisit resolves strictly through the pet's own visits so a foreign visitId is unreachable. The two visible consequences of reusing the booking form unchanged follow from the recorded decisions rather than surprising them: a past-dated visit opens but cannot keep its date (PRD edge case 4 plus an Open Question), and the form still renders the booking button label on a correction.

test_adequacy.note: Thirteen real tests cover both refusal boundaries, the no-second-visit invariant, identifier tampering, and both ownership mismatches, but nothing pins the persistence call: no test verifies the repository save, and the in-place assertions are satisfied by Spring data binding alone, so deleting the save call from processUpdateVisitForm would leave the suite green even though a correction would then never reach the database.

reviewer_hedging.note: The round-2 roster (code-quality, test) approved cleanly and the doc reviewer approved with no findings, but the security approval carries four unretracted recommendations, two of which touch this change: the new state-changing POST inherits the owner mass-assignment surface and the missing CSRF protection, and the supply-chain check is recorded as not run rather than clean.

scope_deviation.note: The diff matches the intake statement point for point, including the two URLs, the unchanged template, and the deliberately absent owner-detail link; the single design revision was a re-triage over uncommitted ADR files failing the autofix audit, not scope drift. The row reports zero build retries because its window opens at the later design-block, while the log holds one records-coverage build failure at line 8 with no code cause.

rationale: The code reads correct and stays inside its triage, but no test pins the repository save on the correction route, so the one line that persists a correction is unprotected. Check that, and note the security reviewer's carried-over mass-assignment and not-run supply-chain caveats.
